characters.description: A Men's Rights Activist influencer and head of theManMadeboot camp, a men's camp that openly promotes misogyny. Abhorrent Alpha Male: He has many traits of a typical Alpha Male and is an egotistical bully who tries to get his clients to be as much of aHe-Man Woman Hateras he is. Actor Allusion: He's basically a modern version of Rex fromNapoleon Dynamite, who was also played by Diedrich Bader. The main difference being that Rex is a self-made man with a wife while Eli is an incel who scrounges off his mother. Hate Sink: He's an open misogynist who runs a program that's dedicated to turning other men into hateful human beings like himself, and the show does little to make his blatant hate speech even slightly comedic. That's not going into the fact that he fleeces vulnerable men out of a ton of money while leaving them worse off in return. He-Man Woman Hater: He outright runs a boot camp all about teaching men to blame women for all their problems.

characters.name: John Redcorn
characters.description: A Native American masseur, one-time rock musician, and the biological father of Joseph Gribble. Aesop Amnesia: In Season 4, the years-long affair he's had with Nancy Gribble ends when she starts falling back in love with Dale. John Redcorn himself feels guilty about betraying Dale's trust when he's only ever been a good friend (and helps John Redcorn get documents that would eventually help him reclaim some of his people's land). By season 6, he is shown to have begun second-guessing his decision, even breaking down in tears in "Sug Night," and making attempts to win her back by season 11.Subvertedin the revival season where it seems that John Redcorn has finally let go of his feelings for Nancy and has settled on just being friends with her and starting a business that was even Dale's idea, with Dale giving John Redcorn his blessing to work with Nancy. John also seems to accept that Joseph sees Dale as his father by calling Joseph his last name, young Gribble. This also had the positive effect of John Redcorn having Nancy and Joseph in his life, with him forming a platonic business relationship with Nancy and Joseph having a more positive relationship with John Redcorn as a family friend and an implied father figure. It seems John Redcorn has truly buried a hatchet with Dale, and a friendship has also been formed with him. Arrow Catch: "Vision Quest" sees him catch an arrow fired by Joseph with his bare hand before it can hit and kill an innocent panda. Berserk Button: Hereallydoes not likeanyone implying a sexual attraction to Nancyin front of him, as Hank finds out in "Sug Night" despite the fact they were no longer having an affair by then. Blatant Lies: One time, he flat-out denies he cheated on Nancy years ago (at the same time that she was cheating on Dale with John Redcorn).John Redcorn:I swear, I don't know any 'Charlene'!

characters.name: Octavio
characters.description: Dale's friend, a vaguely criminal character who helps Dale with some of his shadier activities. Battle Butler: For Dale, though he's really more of a freelancer that Dale hires exclusively. Comic-Book Fantasy Casting: He resemblesDanny Trejo, who would voice Enrique in the show's later years (contrary to popular belief, Trejo never actually voiced Octavio). Cool Old Guy: Has a large tattoo ofRob Zombieon his chest (as opposed to Danny Trejo's tattoo of a beautiful senorita). Villainy-Free Villain: Deliberately invoked. He looks and acts like a tough criminal, but never does anything more serious than minor fraud (like making Hank smash his fender with a crowbar). In "Redcorn Gambles With His Future," he even seems shocked when he thinks Dale wants him tokill a magician so John Redcorn can perform in his place.

characters.name: Buckley
characters.description: Luanne's ex-boyfriend and, much to Hank's displeasure, Hank's superior as department manager at Mega-Lo-Mart. The Artifact: Despitedying at the end of the 2nd season, he's never removed from the opening credits of the first thirteen seasons, even after they were re-animated for High-definition television. The Atoner:His spirit visits Luanne and helps her deal with her grief and get into community college to make up for being such a jerk to her in life. The Ditz: It's vaguely implied that it's because he's getting high all of the time, but he's probably just an idiot. Everyone Has Standards: While generally apathetic to everything and being selfish, he's revolted by Leanne'sattempt to give him a striptease.

characters.name: PJ Finster
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: His daughter is clearly an adopted Asian and it is implied in "Strangeness on a Train" that he and Peggy's coworker are on a date. However, he also says "We decided to leave the wives at home tonight" and (jokingly?) makes passes at Peggy in "The Powderpuff Boys", rubbing her shoulders and making a joke about someone bringing a sleeping bag for multiple people at an activity. However, when Peggy called out that a person should be gay openly, he seems genuinely interested to find out who this person is and unaware Peggy is referring to him. Camp Gay/Camp Straight: His sexual orientation is a mystery, but his level of camp is anything but subtle. Have I Mentioned I Am Heterosexual Today?: If indeed he is gay, his behavior in "The Powderpuff Boys" falls squarely into this category.

characters.name: Appleseed
characters.description: Forgotten First Meeting: He completely forgot about the time he met Hank for one week at the woods and when he was taken into Bill's house as a therapy home guest. Ink-Suit Actor: Resembles his voice actorDave "Gruber" Allen. Odd Friendship: Hank normally hates hippies, but he and Appleseed bond over their shared love for organic farming and specifically cattle. The Thing That Would Not Leave: One of many other troubled adults that were forced into Bill's care until Hank and Bill relocated them all away.

characters.name: Topsy
characters.description: Animal Motifs: He scares people by puffing up his cheeks, similar to a blowfish. Been There, Shaped History:According to Cotton, he murdered Nazi Herman Goering in his prison cell. Bus Crash: He's mentioned as having died offscreen in "Death Buys a Timeshare," being the last of Cotton's war buddies to diebefore Cotton dies for last in "Death Picks Cotton." Rubber Face: His trademark is puffing up his cheeks to enormous sizes, due to the fact he had lost all his teeth. Shell-Shocked Veteran: Implied. Although the VFW guys are very gung-ho about their service and look down on the town'sVietnam veteransfor (admitting to) having PTSD, at one point during an argument between the two groups he wearily admits that he hasn't slept in fifty years.

characters.name: Erwin
characters.description: Odd Name Out: He is the only one of theVDWgang Cotton calls by his full name instead of a nickname like Topsy, Doc, or the multiple Fattys, Stinkys, and Brooklyns. Recurring Extra: He appears four times in seasons 4-6, but mostly in group scenes without much individual focus. Retired Badass: Cotton views him as a potential recruit for a plot to assassinate Castro based on his old exploits, but Erwin needs an oxygen mask to breathe and is unfit for physical work. Uncertain Doom: An inscription with his date of death is shown in season 13, but his first name is spelled with an I instead of an E and, despite appearing in several earlier episodes, he is listed as having died in 1991, six years before the show even started, making it unclear if someone made a mistake with the inscriptions or it was a similarly named character who died.

characters.name: Hal
characters.description: A guy Hank meets at the Mega-Lo Mart while trying to buy a L-pipe, and takes a strong liking to, mainly because they are very alike in personality. Berserk Button: How Hank and Hal met. Neither man gladly suffers the fools at the Mega-Lo Mart. In Hank's case, he is arguing with an associate about finding a L-pipe. Meanwhile, in the same section, an equally frustrated Hal is trying to explain, very loudly, to another associate that drill bits come in different sizes. Heterosexual Life-Partners: For a few days while they get over the excitement of having found a kindred spirit. It's treated in much the same way as a whirlwind extramarital affair, with Bill and Dale as the "jilted" friends, since it would be too out of character for Hank to even consider cheating on Peggy. Another parallel is that Hank is tired of his friends' antics, this time regarding their carelessness with a rented back-hoe, in the same way that a spouse's inconsiderate behavior might be the setup for his/her partner's eyes to start wandering. Ink-Suit Actor: Hal resembles his voice actor, Drew Carey, as he appeared in the late 90s. Meet Cute: A platonic example between two straight men. Their friendship takes off when Hank tries to unlock a red truck identical to his, only to find out it belongs to Hal.

characters.name: Emilio
characters.description: Bobby's right-hand man and voice of reason at Robata Chane. Foil:To Buck Strickland. Buck is an older man who spent the original series as theMean BossHank worked under, while Emilio is an older man who worksforHank's son, Bobby. While Buck is typically aJerkasswho relies mostly on Hank to keep his business afloat to the point of borderline exploitation, Emilio is aNice Guywho encourages Bobby to make the most of his natural talent and is a very talented and competent cook in his own right.Also a foil to Hank, in that he turns out to be (a part of) the glue that holds Robata Chane together, as Chane finds out the hard waywhen he fires Emilio for trying to take the heat for Bobby's relationship with Connie. Chane ends upagreeing to hire Emilio back, with a raise. To Buck Strickland. Buck is an older man who spent the original series as theMean BossHank worked under, while Emilio is an older man who worksforHank's son, Bobby. While Buck is typically aJerkasswho relies mostly on Hank to keep his business afloat to the point of borderline exploitation, Emilio is aNice Guywho encourages Bobby to make the most of his natural talent and is a very talented and competent cook in his own right. Also a foil to Hank, in that he turns out to be (a part of) the glue that holds Robata Chane together, as Chane finds out the hard waywhen he fires Emilio for trying to take the heat for Bobby's relationship with Connie. Chane ends upagreeing to hire Emilio back, with a raise. Gun Nut: His first solution to a rat problem is to pull out a pistol (much less bringing a pistol to a kitchen) as well as claiming that people close their eyes when doing things they love, which is why he does that when at the firing range.

characters.name: Willow
characters.description: Abusive Parents: She mentions offhand that her late father became an abusive alchoholic after losing his job at the Cowboys' stadium, though never elaborates over what type of abusive he was.She blames Jerry Jones for this and has been looking for the chance to deface his property for years as revenge. Betty and Veronica: The outspoken Veronica to Connie's mild-mannered Betty, with Bobby as the Archie. Dating What Daddy Hates: Zig-zagged with her relationship with Bobby. Willow has dyed hair that's shaved on one side (After Hank hadcomplained multiple times about exactly that), is into natural home remedies, and is strictly Vegan. This isn't intentional on Bobby's part as much as it is their natural chemistry, but Hank clearly hates her at first, and Bobby knows the first dinner with her has the chance to end in disaster, especially when she oversteps a massive boundary by shoving vegan lasagna into Hank's mouth. They get along for a little bit over Willow's football skills, butthe fact she only came to football camp with them to defecate on Jerry Jones' desk ends up making it clear there was no salvaging her reputation in Hank's eyes, and Bobby was so put off by it he broke it off. Excrement Statement: Hank and Bobby walk in on her in Jerry Jones's office as she's preparing to defecate on a picture of him on his desk.She does this because she blamed her father's alcoholism, and possibly his death, on his being fired by Jones. Foil: To Connie. Where Connie is a high-achieving college girl, Willow dropped out of college after a year in favor of starting her own business, believing college to be a waste of money (as Bobby has also expressed), and is more laid-back compared to Connie. Conversely, Willow holds slightly more conservative views on dating and sex than Connie does, dismissing ethical non-monogamy as an excuse for college girls to get "side dick."Act surprised when this isexactlywhat Chane was taking advantage of himself on Connie rather than her doing it fo

characters.name: Ola
characters.description: Connie's roommate at UT-Dallas, and a friend to Bobby. Black Best Friend: To Connie, as her main support system outside of Bobby. Everyone Has Standards: She brushes off Joseph's awkward attempts at a pick-up line. Do You Want to Copulate?: Outright asks Bobby if he wants to hook up with her, which surprises him.

characters.name: David Veal
characters.description: A former student of Peggy Hill who is now a food critic for the Dallas Daily News. The B Grade: David resents Peggy because she gave him an F on an essay onBeowulfand it resulted in him being denied admission to Vanderbilt University. Caustic Critic:Initially defied by David, as when he learned that Robata Chane was run by Bobby, the son of Peggy Hill, whom he has a grudge against, he initially refused to leave any sort of review for the restaurant because he recognized it would be a conflict of interest. It was only after she went to his office and doubled down on her being in the right that he then left a scathing review. I Hate Past Me: As Peggy goes over Dave'sLiterature/Beowulfessay, he gradually looks more and more ashamed of how amateurish his writing was. It's Personal: Turns out to be this when David learns that his old substitute teacher in high school is the mother of the chef of the restaurant (Bobby), he decides not to do the review. He claimed it is because of a "conflict of interest", but it is revealed to be because he claims Peggy didn't grade his high school essay fairly.

characters.name: Isabel
characters.description: The producer of the "reality" cooking show,King of the Grill Corrupt Corporate Executive: Downplayed, but it's clear that she is after TV ratings from Bobby's appearance onKing of the Grill, regardless of the human cost to Bobby, his staff, or his relationship with Connie. It's strongly implied that she fired Bobby after he made an on-camera declaration of love for Connie, when she had pressured him to accept Claire's advances so that she could sell the show as a romance story. Kayfabe: She prefers to create drama in order to increase viewership, and doesn't mind if the drama is fake. In her first appearance, she encourages Bobby to be verbally abusive towards his staff, which Bobby and his staff are clearly uncomfortable in doing, after she witnesses Bobby venting his frustration over being rejected because his kitchen is well-run and largely drama-free. She also encourages Bobby to play up an on-screen relationship with his cooking partner, Claire, even though he is fully committed to Connie and worried that Claire's unwanted advances might cause Connie to break up with him. She also lets slip the celebrity chef she has judging the show lost his sense of taste due to Covid, meaning a chef's actual merit in their cooking show has nothing to do with the quality of their actual cooking.

characters.name: Rooster
characters.description: Operates a crime ring out of Hot Springs, Arkansas. He runs a backroom gambling den in Hot Springs, and later runs an illegal food truck in Arlen during the trans-fats ban. Corrupt Hick: Between running a gambling den and an illegal food truck that doesn't even try to meet minimum standards of safety, Rooster makes Buck Strickland, M. F. Thatherton, and Lane Pratley look honest by comparison. Illegal Gambling Den: Runs one of these in Hot Springs, where Buck is a regular patron. Lethal Chef: An almost literal example, as his food trucks were so filthy that customers were getting salmonella from his food. Literal in another way, as his goons have no problem physically assaulting competing food-truck operators. The Mafia: While not known to be affiliated with the actual Mafia, he does run a small-time organized crime ring.

characters.name: Alabaster Jones
characters.description: The Cameo: Appears as one of theNPCsinPro-Pain, the MMO game in "Grand Theft Arlen". Chase Scene: He has a memorable car chase with Hank, Peggy, and Tammi. Know When to Fold 'Em: When Hank made a defiant stand to prevent Tammi from being taken, Alabaster simply stops, especially when Hank paid him off with the money Tammi earned when she went back to prostituting herself. Alabaster accepts, but when he sees Peggy and asks how much to pay for her (he mistook her as another prostitute as she was made to dress like a prostitute beforehand by Tammi) and Hank refuses as he asserts that he and Peggy are married, Alabaster leaves only after telling Hank "that's the biggest mistake a pimp can make, marrying one of his 'hos". Meaningful Name: He is likely called Alabaster because he is white and wears all-white pimp attire. His Cadillac is white as well, with gold rims. The Napoleon: Rather slight in stature, but aggressive.Tammi:Alabaster's a little guy, but he'll mess you up.Hank:No offense, but he's fromOklahoma.
